task.name: Reviewer re-inclusion — restore a deprioritized reviewer after clean attempts (inverse of #1388)
task.story_text:
## Observed / motivation

`assignment.py` deprioritizes a reviewer whose attempt-completion history is poor (the reviewer completion-rate rerank landed in #1388): the reviewer is sorted below higher-completion candidates. There is no landed mechanism that *re-includes* a deprioritized reviewer once its subsequent attempts complete cleanly. The deprioritization is a one-way ratchet.

This is one of the open asymmetries catalogued by the routing-symmetry invariant (#1389). #1388 (reviewer attempt-completion profiles) has landed, so this inverse is now actionable.

## Why

Without a re-inclusion path, a reviewer that recovers its completion reliability stays permanently deprioritized on the strength of old failures — the same promotion-without-demotion failure mode the routing-symmetry invariant exists to prevent, but on the reviewer axis.

## Acceptance criteria

- A deprioritized reviewer is re-included (restored to normal ranking) once a defined number of subsequent attempts complete cleanly.
- The re-inclusion trigger is a named, documented condition (K consecutive clean attempts, or an equivalent recovery rule).
- The routing decision audit records when re-inclusion fired (or was checked and did not), consistent with the routing-symmetry audit-attribution requirement.
- Tests cover both directions: a reviewer deprioritized for poor completion, and the same reviewer re-included after clean attempts.
- The `ROUTING_SYMMETRY_REGISTRY` entry (currently `open_followup="reviewer-reinclusion"`) and `docs/routing-symmetry-followups.md` are updated to pair the deprioritization with this landed inverse.

## Example

Reviewer X fails to complete 3 of its last 5 attempts and gets deprioritized. Over the next 5 cycles it completes every attempt cleanly. With this mechanism, after K clean attempts X is re-included at its normal ranking; without it, X remains deprioritized indefinitely on the strength of the old failures.

Follow-up to #1389 (routing-symmetry invariant). Companion to #1388 (reviewer attempt-completion profiles).

handoff.summary: Landed the registered inverse of the #1388 reviewer completion-rate deprioritization as an explicit K-consecutive-clean-attempts recovery rule, with K pinned to the existing reviewer_completion_min_runs sample floor (no new config surface). model_profiles.get_review_signal now returns a `recovery` sub-dict (clean_streak, clean_attempts_required, recovered) computed from the existing ordered _completion_recent ring via a new _trailing_clean_streak helper; all existing counters, raw/weighted rates, floor behavior, taint exclusion and recency weighting are unchanged. assignment._rerank_reviewers_by_completion now treats a below-threshold reviewer as deprioritized only when the recovery condition has NOT fired, and records the recovery check for every consulted reviewer in the completion audit (reinclusion_mechanism, reinclusion_clean_attempts_required, reincluded, reinclusion_checked). _reviewer_completion_check emits a nested reinclusion_check block (via a new _reviewer_reinclusion_check builder) present whenever reviewer completion profiles were consulted, carrying mechanism/fired/clean_attempts_required/reincluded/checked/checked_detail/reason so the checked-but-didn't-fire path is never a silent gap. ROUTING_SYMMETRY_REGISTRY's reviewer pair now names MECHANISM_REVIEWER_COMPLETION_REINCLUSION ('reviewer_completion_reinclusion') as its landed demotion with audit_label 'reinclusion_check' and demotion_tests pointing at the reviewer completion test module, replacing demotion=None/open_followup='reviewer-reinclusion'. docs/routing-symmetry-followups.md moves the entry from 'Open asymmetries' to 'Resolved / not open'. The two rules are not redundant: with the ~50-run recency half-life a reviewer with 20 stale failures still scores ~0.23 after 5 straight clean attempts, so passive decay alone would leave it deprioritized for dozens of runs — a dedicated test pins that premise so the recovery tests cannot pass vacuously.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
